Subject: Token mix & SLA impact — renewal options and term adjustments

Alex — following up on our renewal that’s coming up in Jan. We pulled together a short usage breakdown for Q4 (attached) and a couple renewal scenarios that change the token mix and SLA targets. Quick highlights: 

- Your generative chat traffic (~68% of tokens) has higher p99 latency sensitivity compared with batch embeddings.
- Prefix cache hit rate is around 28% on sessions with repetition; enabling a small KV-cache policy on Dedicated would reduce token spend by ~9–12%.
- If Paragon prioritizes a 99th percentile latency SLA (50–75ms target), that pushes us to higher-reserved capacity vs. a flexible, best-effort plan.

I attached the raw token mix file. Can we sketch what matters most on your side: lower unit cost (token efficiency), stronger p99 SLA, or simpler term (single blended rate)? I’ll copy Ben and Monica who can run the cost permutations.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — useful snapshot. A couple of clarifying Qs before we loop procurement into modeled options: 

1) When you say "KV-cache policy on Dedicated" — is that an extra config we enable on our reserved pool or a different SKU? Any client-side changes required?
2) For the p99 latency numbers, can you show the delta on cost (monthly committed spend) between a 95ms target vs a 65ms target? We want to understand hit to unit economics if we tighten SLA.

High level: Paragon is leaning to keep a single committed contract but we might accept a modest uplift in committed GPU capacity if it buys a guaranteed p99 SLA. Procurement will need a clear mapping from commit size -> p99 numbers AND a fallback plan if usage spikes past commitment (burst credits, ephemeral hosted fallback).

— Alex

Looping in some concrete numbers and the term options PDF (attached). Answers to Alex’s Qs: 

1) KV-cache policy: This is server-side config applied to your Dedicated pool. No SDK changes required; you'll just toggle cache policy per model. It’s included in the Dedicated SKU (no extra license) but higher cache hit assumptions are baked into the committed capacity math.

2) Cost delta for p99 targets (high level):
- 95ms p99 target: baseline commit (what you’re on today) -> estimated commit $78k/mo
- 65ms p99 target: +22% committed GPU capacity -> estimated commit $95k/mo
- 50ms p99 target: +38% committed GPU capacity -> estimated commit $108k/mo

We recommend a hybrid approach: keep a single-year committed contract but include a burst credit pool (48-hour window, auto-billow to Hosted) and a scheduled quarterly review to re-evaluate commit sizes. That gives Paragon guaranteed p99 for steady-state with a soft landing during spikes.

Attachments: redwood_sla-term-options_20271217.pdf (4 pages)

Action items: Naomi — can you confirm if Paragon prefers a blended token rate or model-specific tiers? Monica — I’ll prepare two redlines for the contract team: (A) stronger p99 with burst pool; (B) blended-rate commit with higher headroom but lower p99 guarantee.

— Ben

Ben/Naomi — thanks, that framing helps. Paragon is inclined toward option A (stronger p99 with burst pool). Procurement requests: 

- A one-page summary of the pricing and the fallback operating model we can include in our SOW (we need the language for "burst credits" and failure modes).
- A sample SLA commitment clause with objective measurement windows (we prefer 30d rolling for p99 claims).
- Confirmation that enabling KV-cache policy does not change data isolation guarantees or retention settings.

We’ll run the legal redline early Jan. Tentative internal approval to move forward pending the one-pager and SLA language.

If you can send the summary and DocuSign-ready SOW by Wed 12/22, procurement will target sign-off in the first week of Jan.
